digo: nyanya; mtamata (Pakia); traditional tomato mtindi / tindi
digo_source: Mgombato ('nyanya tomato'; 'mtindi traditional tomato plant'; 'tindi bush tomato'); Pakia ('Mtamata')

teaser.en: Long before the big market tomato, Digo gardens had their own small 'bush tomato', called *tindi*.

summary.en: *Nyanya* is the tomato, grown in gardens and used in kachumbari salad and stews. Digo also has its own words for a traditional, smaller tomato.

about.en: The tomato is a sprawling, hairy herb with strong-smelling, divided leaves and small yellow star-shaped flowers. The fruit is juicy and usually red when ripe. Traditional tomatoes are smaller than the large market kinds.

where.en: Tomatoes are grown in home gardens on the south coast.

uses.en: Tomatoes go into *kachumbari*, the fresh onion and tomato salad served with many coastal meals, and into stews.

names.en: The Digo word is *nyanya*, the same as in Swahili, and Pakia records *mtamata*. The traditional tomato plant is *mtindi*, and its fruit, the bush tomato, is *tindi*. In English it is tomato.

mgombato: mtindi2 (mi) traditional tomato plant; mnyanya wa kienyeji.
tindi (-) bush tomato; nyanya za kienyeji.
sources: Mwalonya, Nicolle, Nicolle & Zimbu, Mgombato: Digo-English-Swahili Dictionary (BTL / Digo Language and Literacy Project, 2004; e-version 2005)

Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: An ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD diss., Univ. Bayreuth (Appendix III & Table G.2) https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
